aboutGlc.title: Legacy of Government Law College, Mumbai
aboutGlc.description: Established in 1855, Government Law College (GLC), Mumbai is a landmark institution in legal education and is recognised as Asia’s oldest law college. With a legacy built on academic excellence, practical legal training, and a commitment to shaping future legal professionals, GLC has played a defining role in India’s legal landscape.

aboutIprc.title: About the IPR Cell
aboutIprc.mission: The college inaugurated the Intellectual Property Rights Cell (IPRC) in the academic year of 2023-2024 to illuminate students and innovators with a thorough understanding of intellectual property rights. By nurturing a self-sustainable environment that thrives on innovation and creativity within the college ecosystem, the Cell bridges classroom learning with real-world practice.

keyPillars.title: Academic Rigour & Research
keyPillars.description: Annual double-blind peer-reviewed IPR Journal published in academic partnership with leading databases like Manupatra and CaseMine.

keyPillars.title: Advocacy & Moot Simulations
keyPillars.description: Host to India's premier Trademark Opposition Competition (TOC) commemorating the legacy of Prof. Tehemtan N. Daruwalla.

keyPillars.title: Executive Certificate Courses
keyPillars.description: Intensive weekend programs instructed by senior partners and IP heads of Khaitan & Co, Mulla & Mulla, Trilegal, and Fox Mandal.

keyPillars.title: Pro Bono IPR Clinic
keyPillars.description: Connecting student researchers with emerging innovators, artists, and creators for grassroots intellectual property literacy.

principal.name: Dr. Asmita A. Vaidya
principal.quote: It gives me great pleasure to present the work of the Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Cell of Government Law College, Mumbai. Established to create awareness and build capacity in the field of Intellectual Property, the Cell has been actively engaging students through seminars, workshops, and certificate courses. As Asia’s oldest law college, GLC has always been committed to academic excellence and practical learning. The IPR Cell furthers this legacy by equipping students with the skills and knowledge to meet the evolving challenges of Intellectual Property law. I congratulate the Cell for its efforts and am confident it will continue to inspire innovation and contribute meaningfully to the legal community.

founder.name: Gaurav Lokhandani
founder.quote: I watched it happen too often — batchmates and seniors writing off IP as a career before really giving it a chance, assuming it did not pay or did not matter. In law school, IP rarely went beyond the syllabus. Businesses carried the same blind spot, treating IP as something to sort out later, after there was actually something worth protecting. By then, someone else had already filed the mark, already owned the idea. That is why I started the IPR Cell in 2023, to make at least a few students look twice. The ones who take IP seriously now will be the ones protecting it later, in boardrooms, in courtrooms, and in businesses of their own.
